title: The Belly of the Beast
subtitle: In Which Waluigi Watches Five People Walk Into A Mouth On Purpose
filed: 30 Harvestide, 1040 BF — filed from the desk, afterwards, at length
pullQuote: The correct plan was said out loud, by Archie, thirty seconds after the mask came off. It was run. Nobody voted it down. He simply talked himself out of it.
standfirst: Waluigi was not in that grove and will be saying a great deal about it anyway. The full night: the healer taken first, the mask coming off at zero inches, a wizard welding the only door shut, a horn heard for fifty miles, and a stump at the bottom of a pit that this party has stood at before.

sections.heading: They Went For The Healer First And Nobody Has Said It Out Loud
sections.body:
Waluigi was not in that grove. Waluigi wants that on the record at the top, because this is going to be four thousand words of opinion and the reader deserves to know the opinion is coming from a desk.

Here is what happened. The crows came off the branches all at once and the sound was not a caw — it was a dry leathery clatter, a thousand playing cards shuffled at speed, and it went up into the dark, bent sideways, and came down on Feyward Dan.

He got one arm up. Waluigi wants the reader to understand that this is the whole warning anybody received. That was the entire amount of time there was.

The mass closed over his red cap and his mail and the shape of him stopped being a shape. Beaks on steel, WORKING THE GAPS IN THE RINGS. He said "GET OFF —" and stopped saying anything at all.

The birds lifted in one unhurried spiral and Feyward Dan came down on his face in the mud at Archie's boots. His fingers moved once and did not move again.

Now. Waluigi is going to be the one to say the thing.

**That was target selection.**

Three engagements this squad has fought against that scarecrow. Three. And it opened the fourth by taking the healer off the board before it touched anybody else — not the wizard who keeps setting fire to its property, not the enormous man on the motorbike, not the centaur with the warhammer. The PALADIN. The one who puts people back together.

Waluigi has read that sentence back six times. That is not a swarm finding a body. A swarm finds whatever is nearest and loudest. This came off the branches ALL AT ONCE and went past four other people to reach one specific man.

Something in that grove has been WATCHING them fight, and it has worked out which one to remove first, and it has been patient about it across three separate engagements while everybody in the party filed it as a prankster in a hat.

*WAH! Waluigi has read the previous three filings. Waluigi wrote unkind things in two of them about a scarecrow that makes jokes. Waluigi would like those unkind things reclassified as UNDERESTIMATES.*

Waluigi will come back to the crows. And then Archie shouted "SALAM," and a mushroom-capped Toad who had been safely behind a fallen trunk forty feet back did the arithmetic out loud in a voice half an octave too high — *"Alright — but keep that thing distracted. It's kinda scary"* — and then went anyway.

Waluigi wants the running described accurately. He ran badly. Low, hunched, arms tucked, the way people run when they expect the sky to be the thing that kills them. He hit his knees in the mud so hard he skidded.

Waluigi has a great deal to say about the tactical decisions in this file, and Waluigi has been saving most of it and almost all of it is critical. This is the exception. Salam crossed forty feet of open ground under a bird that had just proven what it does to armour, in order to reach a man who could not thank him, and he said *"Your service won't go in vain"* to somebody who was still breathing. Which is either the wrong thing to say or the truest thing anybody said all night.

sections.heading: Archie Attacks The Ground. Again. It Is Still Not Standing On It.
sections.body:
*"I'm doing something really risky,"* Archie announced.

Nobody had time to ask which part, which is the correct summary of Archie Miser's entire career.

He ran, stopped dead ten paces out, reversed the staff and drove it into the earth like a man setting a fence post. And the ground ANSWERED — the whole floor of the grove humped and split, roots tearing up pale and wet, stones standing on end.

Waluigi will admit this freely: as a piece of spellwork that is GENUINELY IMPRESSIVE, and Waluigi does not hand that out.

And then the Scorncrow — and Waluigi enjoyed this far more than he should have — watched the whole thing happen. Then it laughed — a wet comfortable sound, like a boot pulling out of mud — and said *"Oh, you little thing."*

And the crows came in under its arms. A dozen at each shoulder. They took it up off the buckling earth and it hung there with its heels a foot clear of everything Archie had just spent his considerable talent breaking, coat-tails swinging gently over ground still shaking itself apart underneath.

**This is the SECOND TIME.**

Waluigi has the previous filing RIGHT HERE, open, on the desk, next to the tea. Archie has now attacked that thing's relationship with the ground TWICE, and the thing has demonstrated TWICE that it does not have one. The crows are NOT SCENERY. They are not atmosphere. They are not a spooky mood the Shadowfell puts on. **They are the landing gear.**

Waluigi will put it in one sentence for the tacticians. Until somebody grounds the birds, every tremor Archie casts is an expensive way to redecorate a field.

Then it tipped its sacking head to one side — politely, the way you do with a child — and said *"Care for a swing?"*

Above Remi, a branch turned. It came down on a slow creaking arc, thick as a man's thigh, and the end had been split lengthwise into a point. Four feet of pale splintered wood, descending exactly where a person's chest would be. Waluigi hates this file.

Now Waluigi has to describe what the wizard did next. Archie did not shout a warning and he did not dodge. He ran three steps, jumped, and hit the Scorncrow with his shoulder and every pound he had.

And here is the sentence in this file that Waluigi cannot get comfortable with: **he knew, leaving the ground, where the thing was going to land.** Remi was standing right there. He could SEE her. He connected anyway.

Waluigi is not going to call that wrong. A four-foot spike was already falling and the arithmetic was ugly whichever way it broke. Waluigi is simply going to note that a grown wizard made a decision about a fourteen-year-old's odds in the air, in under a second, without telling her — and that the record should say so plainly rather than calling it heroism and moving on. *"I'll make sure it's worth it,"* he said afterwards. To nobody.

sections.heading: Point-Blank Range, And The Thing Under The Face
sections.body:
The Scorncrow went over backwards. It did not fall the way a person falls — it FOLDED, slow and wrong, more sailcloth than body, and it came down across Remi Akamatsu and put her flat in the mud underneath it.

Waluigi notes the choreography, because it matters: forty feet away Wario was hauling on the buried motorbike while shadow servants closed around him in a ring, and he did not look up ONCE.

Waluigi's favourite moment in the file happens here and nobody has ever mentioned it. Eager came in on the fallen scarecrow with the Shadow Blade lit and brought it down in a flat silver arc — and stopped it mid-swing, whole body twisting to kill the momentum. The tip passed a hand's width over Remi's shoulder. He backed off three steps breathing through his teeth.

Waluigi would like a moment of appreciation for that, because it is the single most difficult physical act in this entire document and it produced no damage, no kill, and no glory. Stopping a committed swing is harder than landing one. He did it because the alternative was in the way.

Underneath several hundred pounds of straw and wet coat, Remi took stock.

*"Well, I have this monster on top of me. I'd better get him off of me."*

*"Preferably push him onto the tremor I made earlier,"* Archie called — and Waluigi wants to bottle that, because a man whose spell has failed twice is on a battlefield RECOMMENDING IT AS TERRAIN.

She got a shoulder into it and shoved, and Waluigi already knows how this goes because Waluigi has read the weight of that thing. *"It's too heavy."*

And then she went quiet. When she spoke again it was flat and small and entirely practical — the voice of somebody who has run out of options and found the last one lying on top of her.

*"Wait a minute. I'm at point-blank range."*

She worked the musket up between her chest and the thing's face, pressed the muzzle into the sacking, turned her head away, and fired.

Waluigi has fired one of those indoors and can report on the noise. The bang went flat and huge. Grey powder smoke rolled sideways. The burlap mask came off ENTIRE, tumbling through the smoke trailing straw and one loose thread, and landed face-up in the mud six feet away with its painted stitched grin pointing at the sky.

Underneath it was a face. Pale. Sunken. **Human.** Waluigi has rewritten this paragraph four times. And it was bleeding the way a man bleeds.

Waluigi is putting the jokes down. All of them.

Three filings. THREE. Three times that thing stood in a field and said, in one phrasing or another, *I am not a monster* — and three times this archive wrote the word monster in the very next sentence. Including twice in Waluigi's own hand.

A fourteen-year-old girl pinned under its weight tested the claim at a range of zero inches, because it was the only move she had left, and **THE CLAIM HELD.**

The archive was not lied to. The archive was not LISTENING. There is a difference and it is entirely the archive's fault.

Remi lay under it and looked up at it and did not say anything at all. Waluigi has read that line more times than is professionally useful.

sections.heading: Wario Solves His Problem By Hitting It, Which Is Also His Solution To Every Other Problem
sections.body:
Waluigi has been waiting the whole file for this bit. Wario let go of the motorbike, turned around, and hit the nearest shadow servant so hard it STOPPED EXISTING.

It came apart into a puff of grey ash that hung in the air and drifted. He took the second on the backswing. Same puff, same drift, ash settling on his shoulder-spikes like grey snow.

*"You shadow chumps have nothing on Wario."*

Waluigi has worked alongside that man for a very long time and Waluigi will confirm the following without qualification: he had been ignoring those things for the entire fight because the BIKE was the problem, and the instant the bike stopped being solvable, the things became solvable, and it took him under four seconds. Wario does not triage. Wario simply changes what he is angry at.

Markop came through the rest at a canter with the warhammer swinging low and level, and hooves and hammer put the last of them down into dust. Waluigi notes the centaur cleared more of them than anybody and has not been quoted once. For one moment the grove held nothing upright but the party and the thing they had spent all night failing to pin.

Then — and Waluigi maintains this is the funniest timing in the entire file — the motorbike came free with a sucking crack and Wario was on it and MOVING — full throttle across churned ground, headlamp swinging wild, straight at the place where Remi, Archie and the unmasked Scorncrow all were.

The Scorncrow got up, laughed once with its ruined face, ran three loping strides at the great tree — and the trunk OPENED. A seam split from root to twenty feet up, and behind it nothing at all. Black, and wet rot. It went in head-first and the seam ground shut.

The tree had a mouth.

Nobody said anything for a second, which Waluigi considers the single greatest under-reaction in this archive. A TREE OPENED A MOUTH. Waluigi would still be screaming.

*"Thanks for the ride,"* Archie said, to a motorbike that had not arrived yet.

And then — quietly, and more sensibly than anything he would say for the remainder of the night — Archie said the right thing. If we can't win this, we run. Dan goes somewhere safe. Where is Green T?

**That was the correct plan.** Waluigi will be returning to it. Waluigi wants it in bold because of what happens to it.

Wario spat. *"We can't let him get away."* He jabbed a gauntlet at Dan on the ground. That toad's poisoned. Look at him — he's PURPLE. Send him away.

Then, over the idling engine: *"We should go to the belly of the beast, and uproot it."*

Remi said it plainer, because Remi says everything plainer. If the tree has to die, we go inside and kill it from in there.

And Archie — who has never once in the recorded history of this archive declined an opportunity to set something enormous on fire — stopped arguing for the withdrawal.

Two plans went on the table and they were the SAME PLAN IN DIFFERENT HATS. Wario's uprooting and Remi's arson both required walking into the thing. The third option had already been spoken aloud, by Archie, thirty seconds earlier, and it was the right one.

Waluigi wants that understood. Nobody voted it down. He simply talked himself out of it, because the alternative involved fire and he is who he is.

sections.heading: The Horn, The Self-Repairing Paladin, And Two Catastrophes Delivered As Jokes
sections.body:
They counted heads by torchlight and came up one giant short, and Waluigi would like to open this section by asking where in the WAH Green T went.

No Green T. NO note, NO shout, no enormous footprints leading anywhere — just an absence where the largest thing in the grove had been standing an hour earlier. Waluigi has opinions about that and is saving them for a filing of their own.

Archie — surveying a poisoned Toad, an escaped monster and a sealed tree — proposed that they go and CELEBRATE.

*"Green T has his own agenda,"* Wario said, entirely unworried. *"Maybe he's helping some other way."*

And then — Waluigi loves her for this and also cannot forgive it — Remi found the horn and pressed it.

**WAHAHAHAH.**

It was not a honk. It was Wario's own laugh, brass-throated and enormous, blasting out of a chrome trumpet at a volume that flattened the grass. It bounced off the tree. It came back off the hills BEHIND the tree. Crows went up out of the canopy in three separate places. The sound rolled away downhill through the dark and kept going for a long time.

*"Wow, that's loud,"* Archie said, in the running for least useful observation Waluigi has ever transcribed.

Then he did the arithmetic and his face changed. *"Too loud. Fifty mile radius will hear this."*

Waluigi needs everybody to sit with that number, and Waluigi means SIT. **Fifty miles.** In the Shadowfell. At night. Immediately after a fight the party did not win, next to a tree that eats people, in a plane where at least three separate factions would pay money for this party's location. They announced themselves to every single thing within a fifty-mile circle using a novelty horn shaped like Wario's laugh, and then they went INTO A HOLE.

*WAH! And Waluigi is honest enough to say the horn is magnificent and he would have pressed it too.*

And then, behind them, in the mud — Waluigi did not see this coming and neither did anybody present — Feyward Dan sat up.

Hands flat on his own chest, faint white light going out between his fingers, the peck-wounds closing over as they watched. He got one knee under himself, then the other, stood up wobbling, and announced at FULL VOLUME:

*"IT'S OKAY ARCHIE, I AM HEALED! I used magic and everything"* — and here his voice dropped to almost nothing — *"although I used all of it"* — and came straight back up — *"but it's alright, no need to worry!"*

Then he turned on Wario, pointed, and grinned. *"Wow, this guy is going to be a tough fight. We all should be in this together. You can't handle this on your own."* And then: **"I don't think that was half his power."**

Waluigi is going to slow this right down. Stop. Read those two statements together, because they were said by the same Toad, to the same audience, inside the same thirty seconds.

*I used all of it* — a report on the party's remaining reserves. Zero.

*That was not half his power* — a report on the enemy's remaining reserves. More than double what they just failed to survive.

Waluigi cannot stress this enough. Both are CATASTROPHIC. Both were delivered as a joke, in a cheerful voice, by a man who had been unconscious four minutes earlier. And not one person in that grove changed a single element of the plan.

Wario's answer was to twist the throttle until the engine screamed and ride at the tree. *"NO ONE CHALLENGES WARIO TO A FIGHT AND GETS A-WAY FROM IT!"*

The dark took the headlamp, then the engine noise, then all of it. Waluigi would like it known that he has done almost exactly this and it also did not work.

sections.heading: The Wizard Empties Himself And Welds The Door Shut
sections.body:
*"Dang,"* Archie said.

He cupped his hands. *"REMI! WARIO! WHERE ARE YOU?"* The grove gave him back nothing. Not an echo, not the engine, not a voice. He decided — correctly, for once — that this was the tree's fault.

Inside, it was worse than silence. Remi tried to move her forearm and it STAYED WHERE IT WAS. Grey cabled web, floor to ceiling, in a room with no visible ceiling. The motorbike was not there — not fallen, not stuck, *gone*.

Something came down a strand above her, in stages, with a click at the end of each stage. Waluigi would like the reader to notice that the tree had a spider in it BEFORE anybody went looking for one.

*"Oh no. Please don't."*

She tore her arm free with a sound like fabric ripping, went backwards, and the fangs came down where her shoulder had been. Then she was running badly in the dark and her boot went through a floor of silk and she pitched forward into the web and stuck fast.

Meanwhile — and Waluigi uses that word with real contempt — outside, Archie levelled the staff and put a bolt of fire into the trunk. It hit with a crack. Bark blackened in a patch the size of a shield. **The tree did not react at all.**

He fired again. Same patch, blacker. Nothing else happened.

So the wizard stopped experimenting. WALUIGI WOULD LIKE IT NOTED THAT THIS IS THE MOMENT.

Waluigi has seen men do this and Waluigi has never once seen it end well. He set his feet, planted the staff, and pulled — everything, every reserve he had, weakened as it was in this place, dragged up through his arms into one cast. The light climbed his sleeves. The third eye blazed. And then his eyes went, both of them, pupils gone, **two sockets of open flame** throwing shadows up his own face.

The blast hit and the tree exploded inward, fire running up the inside of the seam, and every peeled strip of bark at the mouth curled in on itself and fused into a solid, smoking, welded scar.

The tree died. The door died with it. Waluigi put his head in his hands.

And Waluigi agrees with what Markop said next. *"What have you done?"* Markop said. *"You've destroyed our only entrance."*

Waluigi has been unkind about Archie Miser for several thousand words now and intends to continue, but fairness first: the fire bolt did nothing and the second bolt did nothing, and a man who has established that small does not work is not being reckless when he tries large. He was ALSO the one who said run, and got overruled, and was now standing outside a tree with two friends inside it and no door. What he did next was the only lever he had left, and he pulled it with everything he owned.

It just happened to be the WRONG LEVER, and Waluigi says that with sympathy, which is not a word he uses about wizards.

And then — this is the part Waluigi keeps circling — Markop took hold of a loose plate of bark at the seam and pulled it away, and **the jaws SLAMMED SHUT.**

Fire bolt: nothing. Second bolt: nothing. Everything he had: the tree dies and the door welds itself closed. One plate of bark pulled by a centaur: the opening gets smaller AGAIN.

Two men, opposite methods, one minute apart, and the way in narrowed both times.

Waluigi has stopped thinking of it as a door that is jammed. *WAH! A jammed door does not get tighter every time you disagree with it.*

Somewhere on the other side, in the dark, Wario started running. Waluigi hopes he was running toward something.

sections.heading: The Interior Log, In Which It Kills The Wheels Before The Man
sections.body:
Waluigi is changing register for this section. What happened inside is a combat log and Waluigi is going to file it as one, because the people in it did not have the luxury of a story.

The Scorncrow came out of the dark already multiattacking. And it did not go for the man.

**It went for the MACHINE.** Waluigi had to stop reading.

*Murder of Crows*, twice — fourteen points torn out of a thing made of STEEL. Chrome went. Spokes went. Waluigi felt that from another plane. Then it turned on the owner: seventeen and thirteen, and Wario vanished inside a column of wings. Then *Shadow Jump*, and it was simply not there.

Waluigi wants everybody to look very hard at the order of those actions.

It attacked **the wheels before the rider.** Something in that tree identified this party's only means of leaving and destroyed it before laying a single claw on the man sitting on it, and then it teleported clear before anyone could answer.

Waluigi has spent three filings describing that thing as a prankster with a scythe and a bad attitude. **It is a tactician.** It removed the healer in the field and it removed the transport in the dark, and it has been taking notes on this party for three engagements while the party took notes on its jokes.

And then, because one tactician was not enough, the grove joined in behind it and came in BOLD, and BOLD is a MORALE RATING, not a compliment. *Ettercap morale: BOLD (84).* Multiattack, and a dash straight at Remi, long limbs moving over the web faster than anything with that many joints has any business moving. *Giant Green Spider: BOLD (84)* — a Web at a guard, DC 12 Strength, and the man went over sideways with his legs bound to his chest. A second spider rushed the same guard and webbed him again where he lay.

Waluigi has never seen a monster change its mind mid-turn before. The ettercap broke off Remi, dashed at Wario, changed its mind, spun, cast *Web Strand* at the guard — DC 12 Dexterity — and *Reeled* him in on the line as a bonus action, hauling a grown man across the floor ON A ROPE OF SPIT.

Then it went back for Remi and webbed her. Twice.

And then a line Waluigi has read twenty times and still does not like. *Wario retreated from Remi's position.* The log gives no reason but one word: morale.

Waluigi is not going to editorialise about that beyond noting it is in the record, it is unlike him, and something in that tree does things to people's nerve.

And then the guard. Flat on his back, wrapped twice, dragged in on a string, **with no name recorded anywhere in this entire file** — got an arm loose, set the spear, and put five points into the ettercap standing over him.

Waluigi wants a moment of silence for that spear. That is the only friendly attack in the whole interior log. The only one. Everybody with a name was webbed, ambushed, or retreating, and the single blow struck for the party came from a man this archive cannot identify.

*WAH! Somebody find out what that guard is called. Waluigi is not asking.*

sections.heading: They Dropped A Torch Into A Hole And The Hole Objected
sections.body:
Waluigi does not know how you reopen a door a wizard has welded, but a centaur does. Markop got both hands into the welded seam and PULLED. Wood shrieked. The jaws came apart maybe four feet and stayed there, quivering, held open on a centaur's shoulders.

Inside was darkness. He put his head into it and looked down, and the darkness kept going — past the roots, past anything a torch could reach, a shaft dropping away into the ground under the grove.

*"Anyone have a rope?"* Markop asked — nine minutes into a plan whose entire premise was going down a hole, which tells Waluigi everything about the planning phase.

*"I don't think soooo,"* said Dan, who had been conscious for about nine minutes.

So they measured it the way Waluigi would have measured it, which is the way you measure a hole when you have nothing to measure it with. Somebody lit a torch, leaned over the gap, and dropped it in.

Waluigi approves of the method. It is the only piece of experimental procedure anybody attempted all night. They waited for the sound of it landing. **IT NEVER CAME.**

Inside, though — in the dark, in the webs — Remi heard something else entirely. Voices. Several of them. Close, panicking, talking over each other:

*"There's a fire —"*
*"Someone is causing a fire —"*
*"They're going to burn us all down!"*

And then — and Waluigi wants a drum roll — the torch came back out. Not up through the jaws where it went in. It popped out of a split in the TRUNK, six feet to the left, and dropped smoking into the mud at Markop's hooves, still lit.

Nobody outside heard a single word of it. Waluigi wants that failure recorded as a failure of the WOOD, not of the party. They looked at a returned torch and read it as a pit being unhelpful.

Waluigi needs to slow down here, because this is the most important thing in the file and it went past everybody at the time.

**Somebody in that hole said *us*.** Waluigi would like everyone to read that word again.

Not a shriek. Not noise. Not an animal reacting to heat. A PLURAL. Whatever is down there can hear a fire, work out that a PERSON caused the fire, guess what that person INTENDS to do with it, and describe itself as a group with a shared fate.

That is four separate cognitive acts, and Waluigi has met nobles who manage fewer. The last one is the one that should keep people awake. *They're going to burn us all down* is not fear. It is a POLITICAL statement. It has a WE in it.

The party dropped a torch into a pit expecting to learn the depth, and instead received a coherent objection from a community, and only one of them was on the right side of the wood to hear it — and she was stuck in a web at the time and could not tell anybody.

Then Markop set the marching order, and he gave his reasons out loud, which is more than anybody else managed all night:

**Feyward Dan** — paladin, front. **Eager** — scout. **Archie** — squishy, middle. **Salam.** **Markop** — rear, and the rope is his.

Waluigi has criticised a great many decisions in this document and will not criticise this one. That is a correct marching order, stated with reasons, by the only person present who thought to state reasons at all. Armour at the front, the fragile one in the middle, the strongest at the back holding the only way home. Waluigi has been in parties that never worked this out across an entire campaign.

He braced against the trunk, took two turns of hemp around his own barrel, and paid it out hand over hand into the hole.

sections.heading: Markop Puts A Hand On A Stump And The Whole File Changes
sections.body:
Markop's hooves came down on grey earth, and he stopped.

He did not stop the way you stop in a new place. He stopped the way you stop in a room you have been in before and did not expect to be in again — weight going back off the front hooves, head coming up, one long look across the whole span of it before saying anything at all.

*"I know this place."*

Waluigi's tea went cold for the second time this week.

Nobody answered him. Because nobody else did.

Nobody answered him, and Waluigi thinks that silence is the loudest thing in the file.

There was no sky. That was the first thing. Overhead, the ribbed inner wall of a trunk going up into green-grey murk — and under it a whole dead forest, inside a tree that had been growing in a field an hour ago. Wrapped creatures, beast and man, turning slowly on their threads. Some the size of a dog. Some not.

Markop was not looking at the bundles.

He was looking for something, which Waluigi did not understand on first reading and cannot now un-see. He walked forward eight or nine paces with the rope still over his shoulder, past the roots, and stopped at a broad flat stump about four feet across, its top scarred pale where an axe had once gone in and been pulled back out.

He put a hand flat on it.

**THIS WAS THE SILENT GROVE.**

This was the stump they piled the loot on the night they put the Arachnid Matriarch down. The War Mage's Staff that Markop claimed on Archie's behalf and carried out himself. The Web-Woven Scale. The three healing potions Rodger grabbed like a man counting his own heartbeats.

Same grove. Same tree. Same stump. Waluigi checked the loot list twice before letting this sentence stand.

They walked out of that place in daylight, through open woodland, on Raventree Manor's northwestern boundary. They had just come back into it on a rope, through the jaws of a scarecrow's tree, in the Shadowfell.

*"This is the Silent Grove,"* Markop said. *"We cleared it."*

Waluigi has to stop being funny for a paragraph.

Waluigi FOUGHT there. Waluigi froze web strands with ice magic and cut frozen corridors through that silk so the party could move without announcing itself to every spider in a quarter-mile. Waluigi has called that battle his finest hour in print, repeatedly, at length, to people who did not ask.

And Waluigi has to write this next part carefully. It is INSIDE something now. A place Waluigi helped clear, that you used to reach by WALKING, is now at the bottom of a pit inside a monster that was standing in a field an hour ago.

One centaur with a good memory is the only reason this archive knows that, and Waluigi does not enjoy owing anybody this much. Nobody else recognised it. If Markop had been at the front of the marching order instead of the back, or had been webbed like the others, this file would have recorded a NEW LOCATION and the archive would have been wrong in a way it might never have caught.

*WAH! And the question is not whether the grove moved. The question Waluigi cannot put down is whether it was ever only in ONE PLACE — and what else that this party has cleared is still where they left it.*

sections.heading: A Centaur, A Motorbike, And The Only Objective That Mattered
sections.body:
Remi loosed an arrow at a spider and missed, and the shaft went off into the webbing and made NO SOUND LANDING, which tells Waluigi everything about the acoustics of that place.

*"It seems like I hear someone yelling,"* she said.

*"WHERE ARE YOU!"* Markop shouted, and the grove ATE IT — the same way it ate sound the first time, silk taking the edges off every noise until shouting is a thing you do for your own benefit.

Archie stood at the bottom of the rope and thought about spells, which is what a wizard does when he has spent every single one of them. Waluigi would enjoy this more if the man had not spent them on welding the exit shut.

Then — Waluigi did not expect a punchline this late — Markop found the motorbike.

Waluigi did not expect this and neither did Markop. It was lying on its side in the roots at the foot of the great tree. Headlamp cracked, chrome dulled with dust, **PERFECTLY INTACT.** The thing the Scorncrow tore fourteen points out of, the thing that vanished into the dark with Wario on it, was sitting there whole.

He stood over it for a while.

He is a centaur. Waluigi is going to be delicate. There is no arrangement of centaur and motorbike that works, and both of them knew it. Waluigi has tried to picture it several times while writing this and each attempt has been worse than the last.

*"If there is a will, there is a way,"* Archie said. Unhelpfully.

Spiders everywhere, on every strand, at every height — and Waluigi has been in that grove and can tell you exactly what that sounds like, which is NOTHING, which is worse. And in among them, moving in a formation that spiders do not use: **Legion soldiers.**
